content.text: Gantry cranes are essential equipment in industrial production and construction engineering, playing a key role in material handling and heavy lifting.

As a professional crane manufacturer, DGCRANE offers a variety of gantry cranes, including Single Girder, Double Girder, Semi-gantry, and Portable types, capable of meeting diverse needs from light workshop applications to large port operations.
This article provides a comprehensive analysis of price ranges, hidden costs, procurement processes, and budget plans to help you make informed purchasing decisions.
Gantry cranes, with their flexibility and adaptability, are widely used in industrial production, logistics, and construction fields.
Different types of gantry cranes are suitable for different scenarios and working conditions; users should select based on their specific needs.
Through these differentiated designs, DGCRANE gantry cranes not only meet diverse application needs but also help enterprises improve overall production efficiency and ensure safer material handling.

Single Girder Gantry Crane is a rail-mounted medium and small lifting equipment, mainly composed of the gantry frame (including Main Girder, legs, and bottom crossbeam), hoisting mechanism, traveling mechanism, and electrical control system.
It uses an Electric Hoist as the hoisting mechanism and travels along the lower flange of the I-beam Main Girder during operation.
The gantry frame can be of box-type or truss-type: the box-type structure has good manufacturability and is easy to fabricate, while the truss structure is lighter and more wind-resistant.

The whole machine is lightweight, simple in structure, and easy to install and maintain, suitable for conventional loading and unloading operations of small and medium Lifting Capacity in outdoor areas such as factories, mines, freight yards, and warehouses.

Double Girder Gantry Crane mainly consists of the gantry frame, trolley, crane traveling mechanism, operator's cab, and electrical control system.
The gantry frame can adopt box-type or truss-type structure, and the Main Girder adopts a double-girder offset rail design.
According to user requirements, the legs can be designed as A-type or U-type.
The operation mode adopts a closed cab, equipped with adjustable seat, insulating floor mat, and tempered glass windows.
According to customer needs, the cab can also be equipped with heating and cooling air conditioning, buzzer, and intercom system.
Power supply options include cable reel or sliding contact line.

A semi-gantry crane is a rail-mounted lifting equipment, mainly composed of a gantry frame (including main girder, legs, and bottom crossbeam), hoisting mechanism, travel mechanism, and electrical control system.
One side of the gantry frame has legs running on ground rails, while the other side has no legs and runs on an overhead rail along the building structure.

A portable gantry crane is a light-duty gantry lifting device, typically composed of a simplified steel frame structure, movable casters, and an electric or manual hoist.
The lifting capacity is generally 0.5t to 10t, commonly used in warehouses, maintenance workshops, and factory production lines for handling small machinery, parts, or molds.

The cost of a gantry crane is not limited to the equipment quote, but also includes several related expenses.
The main influencing factors are as follows.
The equipment itself is the main cost component, including the main girder, legs, travel mechanism, and hoisting mechanism (electric hoist/trolley).
Gantry crane prices vary greatly depending on specifications and structural design.
Parameters such as span, lifting height, lifting capacity, and duty class directly affect the final cost.
: Ranging from a few tons to hundreds of tons.
Higher tonnage leads to higher manufacturing costs and selling prices.
: Larger spans and higher lifting heights require more steel and more complex designs, thus driving up the price.
: Single girder cranes are generally more economical under light to medium loads, while double girder cranes offer greater load capacity and stability, making them more expensive.
When the crane must operate under complex working conditions, special design and material selection are required.
Environments such as high temperature, low temperature, coastal, cleanroom, or explosion-proof significantly increase manufacturing and design costs.
Gantry cranes are large mechanical equipment, usually transported in containers.
Containers are typically 20 or 40 feet, and some oversized components must be shipped as bulk cargo.
Shipping costs are determined by shipping companies and freight forwarders based on freight rates, cargo volume and weight, trade terms (FOB/CIF), and container type (FCL/LCL):
: Includes local port charges, terminal handling charges (THC), documentation fees, seal fees, container pickup fees, lashing, customs declaration, manifest, VGM, and entry fees.
Suitable for bulk orders, with lower unit freight costs.
: Includes local port charges, customs declaration, manifest, VGM, and entry fees.
: Used for oversized or overweight components, quoted based on cargo dimensions.
: Charged as a percentage of the declared value of the goods.
Installation is another key factor affecting total cost.

Understanding these factors helps enterprises effectively balance performance and budget.
